solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Pissed players taking time to show this old instrument

indicators.note: a drunk person is all over the place, so the letters lose their order
to take something on is to add it, so one more piece joins the group

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Drunken musicians somehow manage to play an antique instrument at a gig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pissed' is British slang for drunk, not angry; here it scrambles the musicians plus T.
explanation.definitionFit: A psaltery is an ancient plucked string instrument, much like a zither, mentioned often in the Psalms.

clue.text: Sadly, 'Big Lola' lacks one that's spherical

indicators.note: something sadly done is badly done, so the letters come out in a wrong order
to lack something is to be without it, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one, removed from the fodder

explanation.surface: A woman nicknamed Big Lola is sadly missing someone who is round in shape.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the I out of BIG LOLA and rearrange the six letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: Global means shaped like a globe or ball, so it is a synonym for round or spherical.

clue.text: Drink when getting it up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drink-related remark about sex: having one when getting it up.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is Private Eye smut; the clue is a simple charade of AS and IT turned upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine from Piedmont, so it is an example of a drink.

clue.text: "Leadership from government useless!" industry heads ball

blocks.note: first letter
first letter
first letter
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Business bosses complain that government offers useless leadership.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads' looks like a verb (industry leads a ball) but it picks the initials of the three words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Guidance is direction or advice given to others, which is a synonym for leadership.

clue.text: Regarding former party leader's rambling?

blocks.note: on can mean about, as in a talk on birds
Michael Foot led the Labour Party from 1980 to 1983

explanation.surface: A comment on an ex-leader's speeches being rambling and incoherent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rambling' suggests long-winded talk, but here it means walking in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramblers walk for pleasure, so someone rambling is travelling by walking rather than by vehicle.

clue.text: One who proclaims POTUS should be stuck against tree, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps means maybe so, hinting the letters given are only one possible order

blocks.note: Donald Trump, President of the United States
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A satirical cry that the President deserves to be stood up against a tree, as if for execution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' at the end looks like hedging but signals rearranging the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: A trumpeter sounds fanfares to announce things, and figuratively someone who trumpets loudly proclaims news.

clue.text: Desiderata is cutting whilst screwing

definitions.note: plural Latin noun for a singular English one

indicators.note: screwing means twisting round, so the letters are twisted into a new order
to cut into something is to enter it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheeky note on what one longs for while in bed with someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' looks like the verb joining definition to wordplay, but it is fodder that goes inside the rearranged word.
explanation.definitionFit: Desiderata are things needed or wanted, exactly what someone writes on a list of hoped-for gifts.

clue.text: see 14ac.
(& 24dn.) An erection in the garden for this old copper (live one)?

definitions.text: An erection in the garden for this old copper (live one)?

blocks.note: surface reading: a structure put up in a garden, with a smutty hint
setter's reading: a climbing vegetable grown up a frame, whose first word was an old London policeman and whose second was slang for a coin

explanation.surface: A double-entendre about something erected in the garden for an elderly policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow Street Runners were London's first police; a bean was old slang for a coin, so a copper. The vegetable is a live one, climbing the canes put up for it.
explanation.definitionFit: This climbing plant is grown up a tall frame of canes, and both parts of its name recall old policemen and old coins.

clue.text: In the sack, holding grid carelessly, gets cut

indicators.note: done carelessly means done sloppily, so the letters are thrown into disorder
to hold is to keep within, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: in the sack is slang for in bed
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone in bed carelessly grabs a grid and gets injured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets cut' suggests a wound; it means shortened, as of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: An abridged text has been shortened by having parts removed, so it has been cut.

clue.text: Off-the-cuff remark from old politician following promotion

blocks.note: an ad, an advertisement, promotes a product
a Liberal, the British party that merged into the Liberal Democrats

explanation.walkthrough: 'Promotion' looks like a job rise but means advertising.
explanation.definitionFit: An ad lib is an improvised line spoken without preparation, just like an impromptu comment.

clue.text: Adventurous sailor, topless on bench, not socially acceptable

explanation.walkthrough: Remove the S from SINBAD; a form as a bench is an old British school word.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad form is an idiom for a breach of manners or etiquette, so behaviour in it is improper.

clue.text: Spin: once it worked to attain Trump's objective

blocks.note: to reel is to whirl or spin
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spin' reads as PR but is the dizzying sense; the colon falsely suggests a definition follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitting president seeking another term aims to be voted back into office, which is his goal.

clue.text: Maybe Clare the broadcaster gets stars on show?

indicators.note: maybe suggests uncertainty, so the letters might be in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
Sky is a British satellite TV broadcaster

explanation.surface: A TV presenter named Clare gets celebrities onto her programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stars on show' suggests celebrities on TV; it means stars visible at night.
explanation.definitionFit: When there are no clouds overhead at night, the stars become visible, so the definition describes the answer by its effect.

clue.text: (& 27ac./20ac./7dn.)  Pissed by how bad a garment chosen online, say, looks when actually on you?

definitions.text: how bad a garment chosen online, say, looks when actually on you

blocks.note: first meaning: drunk, in British slang

blocks.clueFragment: how bad a garment chosen online, say, looks when actually on you
blocks.note: second meaning, read literally: clothing looks poorer once put on the body

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pissed' is British slang for drunk. The second meaning takes the idiom literally: online clothes look worse when worn.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone drunk or dishevelled, and read literally it says a thing looks worse when worn.

clue.text: Specialist union's extravagance

fusion is a joining together

explanation.surface: A trade union for specialists spends money lavishly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' reads as a trade union but means a merging of things.
explanation.definitionFit: Profusion means abundance or lavish excess, and extravagance can mean an excessive abundance.

clue.text: Lawyer arranged to take round "one", as the queen once put it?

explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' supplies its shape, the letter O, which joins LAWYER before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Monarchs traditionally spoke of themselves in the plural, as Queen Victoria's 'We are not amused', instead of the singular pronoun.

clue.text: Dollars we endlessly wasted securing the top legal team?

indicators.note: without an end means the last letter is cut off
wasted means ruined or drunk, so the letters are thrown into disarray
to secure is to hold fast, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written, then shortened

explanation.surface: Money squandered hiring the best lawyers money can buy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Law Lords were the senior judges in the House of Lords, Britain's highest court until the Supreme Court replaced them in 2009.
explanation.definitionFit: These senior judges formed the final court of appeal, so they were literally the country's top legal panel.

clue.text: Where 'disloyal' Scots were tragic victims of devious con in fun

taken as written
full means having eaten enough

clue.text: see 14ac.
